stem: Build a right-angled triangle in which $\sin\theta = {=t}$, where $\theta$ is the marked angle. Drag the two legs; a triangle of any size with this sine is correct.
solution: Sine compares the side opposite $\theta$ with the hypotenuse: $\sin\theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$.
Write the target ${=t}$ as a fraction of whole numbers, opposite over hypotenuse: for example $0.6 = \frac{3}{5}$ and $0.8 = \frac{4}{5}$. The opposite side is the top, the hypotenuse the bottom.
You drag the legs, not the hypotenuse. A hypotenuse of 5 with an opposite leg of 3 leaves an adjacent leg of 4 ($3^2 + 4^2 = 5^2$); with an opposite leg of 4 the adjacent leg is 3.
Check the live readout: $\sin\theta = {=t}$. Doubling both legs gives the same sine, because only the ratio of the sides matters, not the size.
notes: Mirrors book Ex 5.1 Q1(a) (write sin of an angle) by running it backwards: the student must know which two sides make a sine in order to build one. used-cosine is mapped to reads-sides-from-other-angle (opposite and adjacent trade places, so sin theta comes out as adjacent over hypotenuse); the same predicate also fires on a plain SOH-CAH-TOA recall slip, which has no misconception of its own in this objective's list. used-tangent means the triangle's opposite/adjacent ratio equals the target, i.e. sine written as opposite over adjacent, so no hypotenuse in the answer. off-target is deliberately unmapped (too many unrelated causes). ratio-at-the-right-angle and ratios-without-a-right-angle cannot fire here: theta is fixed at an acute vertex and the triangle is always right-angled. The 3-4-5 triangle is shared on purpose with the cos template (sin 0.6 and cos 0.8 are the same triangle). Targets 0.6 and 0.8 are reachable with legs 3 and 4 (or 4 and 3); worth a check that the leg handles reach those lengths and that the instrument marks the angle as theta.
